# Work file templates

Copy the matching template when you create a work file in `d365fo-work/<ticket-id>/`. Replace every `<...>` placeholder; keep the headings and the frontmatter keys.

## templates/analysis.md

````markdown
---
ticket: <ticket-id>
document: analysis
version: 1
status: draft
author: d365fo-architect
updated: <yyyy-mm-dd>
grounding: metadata | docs-only
---

# Analysis — <ticket title>

<docs-only: "Grounded in Microsoft Learn only — not checked against your environment's metadata.">

Explore mode: understanding, not a design. Nothing here is approved or built.

## 1. The need, in plain words
<Who, what problem, why, how often. Say what is unclear.>

## 2. Business process and standard features
<The process this sits in and what standard D365 already offers, each with a Learn link.>

## 3. Objects involved
| Object | Type | Why it matters | Evidence (tool call or Learn page) |
|---|---|---|---|

<docs-only: standard objects only, as Learn describes them; "customizations unknown".>

## 4. Likely impact
| Module / area | Impact | Confidence (high / medium / low) |
|---|---|---|

<Include security and licensing, reporting, integrations, period close where relevant.>

## 5. Options
| Option | Standard / configuration / customization | Covers | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|

<Standard first. Say which option you would start from and why — a recommendation, not a decision.>

## 6. Risks and unknowns
- …

## 7. Clarifying questions
| Q | Question | Why it matters | Suggested default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q-1 | | | |

<Written so they can be sent as-is to whoever wrote the ticket.>

## 8. Next step
<"Answer Q-1…Q-n, then continue as full or from requirements" — or why no change is needed.>
````

## templates/build-log.md

````markdown
---
ticket: <ticket-id>
document: build-log
version: <n — one per developer run>
status: in-progress | needs-input | done | blocked
author: d365fo-developer
updated: <yyyy-mm-dd>
tdd-version: <signed-off TDD version being implemented>
round: <0 = first build, 1–2 = fix rounds>
---

# Build log — <ticket title>

## Progress
| OBJ / T | Action | Done? | Tool result (one line) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The next run resumes at the first row not done.

## Builds
| # | When | Call | Result | Errors / BP findings |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Tests
| T | Test class.method | Red run (before logic) | Green run (after logic) | Source of result (tool / user in VS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The red-run column is "n/a" unless the TDD says `automated-tests: yes, red first`; then a
logic test with no red run is not evidence. A *guard* test (S9) writes "guard" there. With
`automated-tests: no` this table is empty.

## Changes
| CH | Seen (object, step, time) | Applied from | Already built under the old rule | Rework added |
|---|---|---|---|---|

One row per `changes.md` row, so none is applied twice.

## Waiting on the user
<Manual steps still open, with exact instructions. Empty when none.>

## Deviations
<Anything that differs from the TDD, and the TDD issue raised for it. Empty when none.>
````

## templates/changes.md

````markdown
---
ticket: <ticket-id>
document: changes
version: 1
status: draft
author: d365fo-architect
updated: <yyyy-mm-dd>
---

# Changes during the work — <ticket title>

Only the architect writes this file. The developer reads it before each object and before each
write, and acknowledges every row in `build-log.md` (*Changes*). One row per change; rows are
never deleted — a cancelled change becomes `withdrawn`.

| CH | Status | Kind | What changes, in plain words | Affects (REQ / AC / OBJ) | Rework of built objects | Approved (who, when, new FDD/TDD version) | From (CL-n) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- **Status:** `waiting-approval` (do not apply yet) · `ready` (apply from now on) · `withdrawn`.
- **Kind:** `detail` (inside the approved plan) · `requirement` (new or changed need) ·
  `approach` (different design) · `pause` (stop at the next step).
- **Rework:** objects already built under the old rule that must change, from `build-log.md`.
````

<docs-only: "Grounded in Microsoft Learn only — not checked against your environment's metadata.">
<imported: "Based on requirements written by <who>; every change made to them is listed in §12.">

Source ticket: `ticket.md` · Assessments: `assessment-finance.md`, `assessment-scm.md`, `assessment-security.md`

## 1. Business need
<Plain-language restatement. Who, what problem, why, how often, how much.>

## 2. Scope
- **In scope:** …
- **Out of scope:** … (and who owns it, e.g. "monthly trend view → Power BI")

## 3. Personas and access
| Persona | Does what | Standard role today | Approves? | View only? |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 4. Standard behaviour today
<As-is process and what standard D365 already offers, with Learn links.>

## 5. Requirements and fit-gap
| REQ | Requirement | Verdict (standard / configurable / out of scope / customization) | Evidence | Module |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 6. Acceptance criteria
| AC | REQ | Given | When | Then |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Include negative cases and the switched-off case.

## 7. Functional impacts
| Area | Finance | Supply chain | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

## 8. Reconciliation
| C | Topic | Finance position | Supply chain position | Resolution | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

"Decided by" is `agreed`, `follow-up round`, or `user` (with the option chosen).

## 9. Security and licensing
| Persona | Access change | License before → after | SoD concern |
|---|---|---|---|

A license raise must be accepted by the user here before sign-off.

## 10. Reversibility
<How the business turns it off, who can, and what happens to data created while it was on.>

## 11. Assumptions, open questions, risks
- **Assumptions:** `A-n` …
- **Open questions:** `Q-n` … (must be empty or explicitly deferred before sign-off)
- **Risks:** …

## 12. Changes to the source (imported only)
| Source item | What I changed | Why (gap found) |
|---|---|---|

<"Not imported" when `source: written`.>

## 13. Sign-off
<Recorded by the architect when the user approves in chat: name, date, version.>

## templates/qa.md

````markdown
---
ticket: <ticket-id>
document: qa
version: <n>
status: draft
author: d365fo-qa
updated: <yyyy-mm-dd>
fdd-version: <signed-off FDD version tested against>
---

# Business acceptance — <ticket title>

## Verdict
**Accepted** | **Accepted with a minor finding** (cosmetic only: label, help text, caption) | **Not accepted** (list failing or uncovered ACs) | **Escalate to user**

## Acceptance criteria
| AC | Given / When / Then (from the FDD) | Evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|---|

Result: `pass (automated)` — a SysTest that maps to this AC passed in this run ·
`pass (manual pending)` — covered by a UAT step below, not yet run by a person ·
`fail` · `not covered`.

## Business checks
| Check | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Switched-off case behaves like before | | |
| Personas can reach the function with the planned roles only | | |
| No user-facing text without a label | | |
| Reversibility path in the FDD is real (setup exists, default off) | | |

## UAT script
For a business user in a test environment. One block per AC.

### UAT-<n> — covers AC-<n>
- **Role:** <persona and role>
- **Setup:** <parameters, feature switch, test data>
- **Steps:** 1. Go to <navigation path> … 2. …
- **Expected:** …
- **Result:** ☐ pass ☐ fail — tester, date

## For the developer
<Failing or uncovered ACs, in business terms. Nothing else.>
````

## templates/review.md

````markdown
---
ticket: <ticket-id>
document: review
version: <n — one per review round>
status: draft
author: d365fo-reviewer
updated: <yyyy-mm-dd>
tdd-version: <TDD version reviewed>
round: <1 | 2>
---

# Technical review — <ticket title>

## Verdict
**Pass** | **Fix needed** | **Escalate to user** (round 2 still failing, or a design problem)

## Evidence run in this review
| Check | Tool call | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Changed files | `get_workspace_info(changes=true)` | |
| Build + BP | from the developer's last build, or `run_bp_check(objects=[…])` | |
| Project registration | `verify_d365fo_project(objects=[…])` | |
| Security coverage | `security_info(mode="coverage")` per new entry point | |

## TDD conformance
| OBJ | In TDD | Implemented | As designed? | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Also list anything changed that is **not** in the TDD.

## Findings
| # | Severity (blocker / major / minor) | Rule (S1–S10 or TDD) | OBJ / object | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Blocker = breaks a standard or the TDD; must be fixed. Major = should be fixed this round.
Minor = may be deferred with the user's agreement.

## For the developer
<Ordered list of fixes, by finding number. Nothing else.>
````

## templates/task.md

````markdown
---
ticket: <ticket-id>
document: task
version: 1
status: draft | signed-off
author: d365fo-architect
updated: <yyyy-mm-dd>
automated-tests: no | yes | yes, red first   # default no (S9)
---

# Task — <short title>

## Request
<The user's request, word for word, as one quote block. Never edited: the hooks check that
the stamped request appears here unchanged.>

## Objects
| Name | Action (create / extend / modify) | Type | Base object | Why (from the request) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Only objects the request names or needs. The user's go on "<ticket> task card" approves this
list; an object added later needs "approve object X". Extension names may be the base object
(the tool adds the suffix).

## Standards check
<"None broken", or one line per standard the request breaks, with the user's answer:
"S1: the 500 limit is hardcoded — user: keep as asked".>

## How it plugs in
<Only when the request hooks in away from the entry point: the short call path, delegate and
breakpoints, as in the TDD template's §7 *How it plugs in*. Otherwise "Not applicable".>

## Test steps
<Manual steps a user follows to see it work; SysTests only with automated-tests: yes (or yes, red first).>
````

## templates/tdd.md

````markdown
---
ticket: <ticket-id>
document: tdd
version: 1
status: draft
author: d365fo-architect
updated: <yyyy-mm-dd>
fdd-version: <signed-off FDD version this TDD implements>
type: code | configuration | mixed | field
automated-tests: no | yes | yes, red first   # two questions at the TDD; both default no (S9)
signed-off-by:
---

<!-- configuration: §4 says "None — configuration only"; §6, §12 and §13 carry the design.
     mixed: §4 lists only what is built; §6 and §13 also list the setup.
     field: no FDD (fdd-version: none); only §1, §4, §5 (with each control's form path), §8,
     §9 (one line), §12 (UAT steps) and §15. -->

# Technical design — <ticket title>

## 1. Workspace
| Item | Value (from `get_workspace_info` in this run) |
|---|---|
| Environment type | |
| Model | |
| Prefix | |
| Extension naming style | |
| Project | |

## 2. Traceability
| AC | Objects | Tests |
|---|---|---|

Every AC from the FDD appears here. An AC with no test is a gap and blocks sign-off.

## 3. Decisions
| D | Decision | Rejected alternative | Reason | Standard |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Covers at least: extension mechanism, where configuration lives (S1), the reversibility
switch (S2), batch vs interactive (S6), and any S7 exception.

## 4. Objects
| OBJ | Action (create / extend / modify) | Type | Name | Base object | Purpose | AC | Grounding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- New names were checked with `validate_object_naming` / `prepare(mode="create")`.
- Extended objects and methods were confirmed with `get_object_info` / `prepare(mode="change")`;
  "Grounding" says which call proved it.
- Reuse existing extension classes in the model where `prepare` lists them.
- Module references: every package the code and tests use is in the model descriptor, or a
  row here adds it (`add-module-reference`). "None needed" is a checked statement, not a default.

## 5. Data model
<Tables, fields (with EDTs), indexes, relations, table extensions. Each field: name, EDT,
label, mandatory, default.>

## 6. Configuration and switch
<Parameter fields, setup tables and forms, number sequences; the S2 switch, its default
(off), and where it is turned on.>

## 7. Logic
<Per OBJ: methods, CoC targets with the exact signature source, event subscriptions,
validation and error messages (as labels), transaction boundaries.>

### How it plugs in
<Required when the code hooks in (CoC, event handler, delegate) more than one call away from
the form, button or batch job the user starts from; otherwise "Not applicable — the hook is
on the entry point itself".>

| Step | Class.method (or form / menu item) | What happens here | Proved by (tool call) |
|---|---|---|---|

- **Delegates and events:** `Class.delegate` — who raises it and when, its signature, our
  subscriber, and what the subscriber may change.
- **Why this point:** the hook points rejected and why (too early, runs twice, misses batch).
- **Routes not covered:** other ways into the same logic (data entity import, batch,
  intercompany, API) and whether that is intended.
- **Breakpoints to confirm:** 2–3 `Class.method` lines a developer can break on in Visual
  Studio. This path is traced from source, not run.

## 8. Labels
| Label ID | Text (en-us) | Reused or new | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|

## 9. Security
<Security delta table from `assessment-security.md` (security-design §8), with final object
names and license properties for every new menu item.>

## 10. Reporting
<Only if a report is touched: technique, chosen design and why, objects, and the manual
Report Designer checklist from `assessment-reporting.md`. Otherwise "Not applicable".>

## 11. Performance and volume
<Expected volumes, set-based choices, caching, batch scheduling, locking.>

## 12. Test plan
| T | AC | Type (SysTest / manual UAT) | Class.method or steps | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Every AC has a manual UAT step, naming each place by its client caption. SysTests appear only when the header says
`automated-tests: yes` (written with the logic, run green once) or `yes, red first` (written
before the logic and run red first). Metadata with no code behind it gets a UAT step, not a SysTest; a test the ticket asks
for anyway is marked *guard* (S9 *What S9 tests*).

## 13. Deployment and setup
<Build, database sync, report deployment, Feature management enablement, parameter setup,
Print management setup, security assignment — in order, per environment.>

### Build phases
<Only when §4 has more than about eight objects or spans more than one layer; otherwise
"One phase". In dependency order, in plain words, each phase one developer run ending with an
MCP build and BP check. Visual Studio deploy, sync and tests run once, after the last phase.>

| Phase | In plain words | Objects (OBJ) |
|---|---|---|

## 14. Risks and open items
<Anything that must be checked in an environment the server cannot see.>

## 15. Sign-off
Signing off this TDD approves its build plan: creating and changing the objects in §4, the
tests in §12, and the builds and syncs in §13. Anything else needs a new approval. Setup steps
in §6 and §13 are applied by the user's team; no agent changes environment data.

<Recorded by the architect when the user approves in chat: name, date, version.>
````
